wizard.access.title: Granting Access to One Light
wizard.access.body:
A new key can reach nothing until you grant it something. Grant one light you can see, so the test shows the whole path working.

Expand the light group and choose **W** on a light for read and write access. A grant on a device covers its entities; a grant on the whole domain covers every light, including ones added later.

If this Home Assistant has no lights, **{{label:wizard.showAllDevices}}** lists every domain. You can grant more later in the permissions tree.

wizard.accessKey.title: Naming the Access Key
wizard.accessKey.body:
The access key is what the agent presents to Phoenix. Its name appears in the audit log and in approvals, so choose one that says which agent uses it.

An expiry ends the key automatically, and it cannot be changed once the key exists. **{{label:wizard.createAccessKey}}** creates the key; if you connect an external app, its secret value appears on the Connect step.

wizard.choose.title: How Your Agent Connects
wizard.choose.body:
Phoenix is installed. This wizard sets up your first agent and ends with a test you can see working.

- **{{label:wizard.choiceChatTitle}}** runs the agent in a chat window inside Home Assistant. You bring an API key from a model provider, or the address of a local Ollama server.
- **{{label:wizard.choiceAppTitle}}** connects an MCP app you already use, such as Claude Code or an IDE, with a bearer access key.

Either way the agent gets its own access key, and the next steps decide what that key may do. Set up more agents later with **{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}**.

wizard.connect.title: Connecting an External App
wizard.connect.body:
Choose your app for the exact command or configuration, with this key's secret value filled in. Copy it now: Phoenix stores only a hash of the key and cannot show the value again. If you lose it, rotate the key for a new one.

**{{label:wizard.testConnection}}** waits for the app's first request. **{{label:wizard.connectLater}}** finishes now and leaves the test for later.

wizard.done.title: Your Agent Is Ready
wizard.done.body:
The key is ready. In [Access Keys](guide:workspace.accessKeys) you can change its persona, capabilities and permissions, and **{{label:workspace.keyActions}}** rotates or revokes it.

An agent reaches only what its key grants, and changes set to confirm wait for you in [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals).

wizard.persona.title: Choosing a Persona
wizard.persona.body:
A persona is a starting set of capabilities: which kinds of tools the agent may use, and which of them wait for your approval first.

The preselected persona is the cautious choice for a first test. Pick another if you already know the agent's job; you can change single capabilities later in [Access Keys](guide:workspace.accessKeys).

A persona never decides which devices the agent can reach. That comes from the access you grant two steps from now.

wizard.provider.title: Setting Up the Model Provider
wizard.provider.body:
Agent Chat sends the conversation to the model provider you choose, using your own account with it.

Pick an account you have already added, or add one: choose its type, enter the API key or the Ollama server's address, and validate it. Nothing is saved until it validates.

**{{label:wizard.tryNow}}** opens Agent Chat on the new key with a test question typed in.

wizard.test.title: Testing the Connection
wizard.test.body:
Send the suggested prompt from your app. Phoenix notices the app's first request and enables **{{label:wizard.next}}**.

If nothing arrives, check that the app has picked up its new configuration (some apps need a restart) and that the address and key match the Connect step.

wizard.try.title: Trying Agent Chat
wizard.try.body:
Agent Chat is open with a test question already typed. Send it and watch the agent work with the light you granted.

The wizard closes once you send your first prompt. Changes that need your approval wait in [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals).

workspace.accessKeys.title: Access Keys
workspace.accessKeys.body:
Every agent connects to Phoenix with its own access key, and the key decides what that agent may do in Home Assistant.

- **{{label:accessKeys.setUpAgent}}** walks you through creating a key and connecting a client.
- Select a key in the list to show it in the windows below: **{{label:accessKeys.cardPersona}}**, **{{label:accessKeys.cardCapabilities}}**, **{{label:workspace.keySettings}}** and the **{{label:accessKeys.permissionsTree}}**, with the **{{label:accessKeys.permissionSummary}}** summing up what it may reach.
- **{{label:workspace.keyActions}}** on the toolbar renames, rotates or revokes the selected key.

Capabilities set to confirm send an agent's changes to [Approvals](guide:workspace.approvals) before anything runs.

workspace.approvals.title: Approvals
workspace.approvals.body:
Approvals holds the changes agents asked to make through capabilities set to confirm. Nothing runs until you decide.

- **{{label:shell.tabApprovals}}** lists the requests. **{{label:approvals.show}}** chooses **{{label:approvals.tabPending}}**, **{{label:approvals.tabHistory}}** or one outcome. Choose a request to see it in **{{label:workspace.review}}**.
- **{{label:workspace.review}}** shows exactly what would change. **{{label:approvals.approve}}** runs the request. **{{label:approvals.reject}}** refuses it, and you can tell the agent why before you confirm.
- **{{label:workspace.requestDetails}}**, from the toolbar, shows the request's access key, capability, inputs and recorded result.
- **{{label:approvals.selectMultiple}}** approves several requests you already know, in the order shown.

Configuration that agents change is recorded in [Changes](guide:workspace.changes), where an earlier version can be put back.

workspace.changes.title: Changes
workspace.changes.body:
Changes keeps a version history of the configuration agents change: automations, scripts, scenes, integrations, helpers and dashboards.

- Choose a change to see the configuration before and after it in **{{label:workspace.comparison}}**. **{{label:workspace.itemHistory}}**, from the toolbar, lists the item's other changes.
- **{{label:changes.restore}}** puts a saved Before or After back after you confirm. The restore is recorded too, so it can be undone the same way.

workspace.logs.title: Logs
workspace.logs.body:
Logs shows what reached Phoenix and what agents said.

- **{{label:shell.tabAudit}}** records requests to Phoenix with their outcome, access key, method and resource.
- **{{label:conversations.title}}** keeps recorded agent conversations, such as Agent Chat sessions.
- Select a record in either log to read it in full in **{{label:workspace.logDetails}}**.

What is recorded, and for how long, is set in [Settings](guide:workspace.settings).

workspace.mesa.title: MESA
workspace.mesa.body:
MESA describes what each device or entity is, so Phoenix can treat it safely: a profile can make a device confirm-only, or put it off-limits, whatever an access key allows.

- A profile can cover a domain, an integration, an area, a device or a single entity. **{{label:workspace.mesaProfiles}}** lists them all; choose one to open it in **{{label:workspace.profileEditor}}**, or start one with **{{label:mesa.addProfile}}**.
- **{{label:mesa.suggestTitle}}** proposes profiles for devices Phoenix recognizes. Nothing is applied until you choose **{{label:mesa.apply}}**.
- **{{label:workspace.orphanedProfiles}}** and **{{label:workspace.advisory}}** appear only while they have findings. Dismissing a notice changes no profile.
- Until **{{label:settings.mesaModeLabel}}** in [Settings](guide:workspace.settings) is **{{label:settings.mesaModeEnforced}}**, most restrictions only warn.

workspace.my.title: My Workspace
workspace.my.body:
My Workspace holds the windows you use most, gathered from the other workspaces.

- **{{label:workspace.addToMy}}** in a window's menu adds it here. It stays in its own workspace too, and both copies show the same selection.
- **{{label:workspace.removeFromMy}}** in its menu here takes it away; closing it only hides it, and Workspace Options reopens it.
- **{{label:shell.agentChat}}** docks here from its own menu. While another workspace is shown, Chat floats over it, and it returns here when you come back. **{{label:agentchat.floatChat}}** undocks it.

workspace.settings.title: Settings
workspace.settings.body:
Settings holds the options that apply to all of Phoenix, in six windows.

- **{{label:workspace.aiProviders}}**: the AI accounts Phoenix uses, model catalog checks and the optional {{label:routing.providerSection}}.
- **{{label:settings.agentcliCard}}**: how Agent Chat behaves.
- **{{label:workspace.homeAssistant}}**: {{label:settings.voiceCard}}, {{label:settings.aiTaskCard}} and {{label:settings.assistCard}} connect Phoenix to Home Assistant's own AI features.
- **{{label:workspace.safety}}**: the {{label:settings.killSwitchCard}}, MESA enforcement and {{label:settings.dataCard}}.
- **{{label:workspace.logsNotifications}}**: what is recorded, and when Home Assistant notifies you.
- **{{label:workspace.general}}**: language, theme, optional features and version information.

**{{label:workspace.findSetting}}** on the toolbar finds a setting and opens the window it is in.
